rules.title: RSO annual allowable rent increase
rules.requirement: For units under the Rent Stabilization Ordinance, rent may be increased once every 12 months by the allowable rent increase percentage published by LAHD.
rules.key_value: Once every 12 months by the allowable rent increase percentage
rules.coverage_text: Rental properties in the City of Los Angeles first built on or before October 1, 1978, and replacement units under LAMC Section 151.28. This includes apartments, condominiums, townhomes, duplexes, two or more single-family dwellings on the same parcel, hotel or rooming-house rooms occupied by the same tenant for more than 30 consecutive days, residential units attached to commercial buildings, ADUs, JADUs, and mobile homes and RVs in mobile home parks.
rules.exemptions: For condominiums and townhomes, the rent amount is not regulated for tenancies that commenced after December 31, 1995. A landlord can apply for a luxury exemption from the RSO.
rules.quoted_span: Rent may be increased once every 12 months by the allowable rent increase percentage

rules.title: RSO ban on additional utility percentage increase
rules.requirement: Effective February 2, 2026, landlords of RSO units can no longer add an additional percentage increase for utilities.
rules.coverage_text: Rental units subject to the Rent Stabilization Ordinance.
rules.quoted_span: Effective February 2, 2026, the landlord can no longer include an additional percentage increase for utilities.

rules.title: RSO additional tenant rent increase
rules.requirement: Effective February 2, 2026, a 10% increase for an additional dependent added to the tenancy is no longer permitted. A 10% increase is allowed for an additional tenant who is not a dependent, and landlords can increase the rent within 60 days of learning about the additional tenant.
rules.key_value: 10% for an additional tenant (not a dependent)
rules.coverage_text: Rental units subject to the Rent Stabilization Ordinance.
rules.quoted_span: Effective February 2, 2026, an additonal 10% increase for an additional dependent added to the tenancy is no longer permitted. However, a 10% for an additional tenant is allowed (not a dependent) if moves into a rental unit: Landlords can increase the rent within 60 days of learning about the additional tenant.

rules.title: RSO vacancy increase to market rate
rules.requirement: Rent on an RSO unit may be increased to the market rate if the tenant moves out voluntarily, is evicted for nonpayment of rent, for a lease violation, for failure to comply with a Tenant Habitability Plan, or per a City Attorney order, or accepts a Tenant Buyout Agreement.

rules.title: RSO rent increase moratorium
rules.requirement: Rent increases were prohibited for RSO rental units from March 30, 2020, through January 31, 2024.
rules.coverage_text: Rental units subject to the Rent Stabilization Ordinance.
rules.quoted_span: Effective March 30, 2020, through January 31, 2024, rent increases are prohibited for rental units subject to the Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO).

rules.title: RSO legal reasons for eviction and no-fault eviction requirements
rules.requirement: RSO tenancies may be ended only for listed at-fault reasons (such as nonpayment or a nuisance) or no-fault reasons (such as owner or family move-in, resident manager move-in, demolition, a government order, or conversion to affordable housing). No-fault evictions require filing a Landlord Declaration of Intent to Evict with LAHD, 30-day or 60-day written notice (some evictions require 120-day notice or up to a 1-year extension), and payment of tenant relocation assistance.

rules.coverage_text: Rental units subject to the Rent Stabilization Ordinance.
rules.quoted_span: Give the tenant a 30-day and 60-day written notice (some evictions require 120-day notice or up to a 1-year extension).

rules.requirement: Every notice to terminate a tenancy for an RSO rental unit must be filed with LAHD within three business days of service on the tenant.
